gen-dafont-neon-gf-port-lligat-slab: Neon draws every letter with one unbroken line width and tall, stamped-metal lowercase, while Port Lligat Slab tucks its letters close with wide porthole counters. Neon glows; the text serif reads like a page.
gen-dafont-neon-outfit: Neon lights up with a flat, uninterrupted line and tall stamped-metal lowercase, and it earns its keep big and short. Outfit, a plain sans of bent-cable curves, stays lower and quieter beneath it.
gen-dafont-neon-plus-jakarta-sans: Glowing tubes meet precise lines here, with Neon standing tall and stamped-looking up top. Plus Jakarta Sans follows in monoline strokes at a lower lowercase height, and that gap in height is what the pair does best.
gen-dafont-neon-sora: Neon glows with tall, stamped-metal lowercase drawn in one uninterrupted line width, and it sets a bright, vibrant tone. But Sora, a sans with a lower lowercase and widely parted curves, would carry long paragraphs with a crisp, geometric steadiness.
gen-dafont-neon-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk reads with open, breathing counters and a ribbon of constant width, a geometric plain sans with a lower lowercase. Neon, by contrast, glows tall and stamped.
gen-dafont-neuropol-cabin: Neuropol brings a digital, futuristic outline feel with its slim, closed letters, while Cabin looks like bent tubing with open terminals. And if the heading shrinks or the body grows, that closed-versus-open difference starts to blur.
gen-dafont-neuropol-dm-sans: Futuristic and digital, Neuropol holds each stroke to one thickness like a drawn cable. DM Sans then offers friendly, wide-set terminals on its s, which is what a sans does best here.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-asap: Slim, digital, outline-like lettering up top, where Neuropol opens its c through a narrow channel. Asap follows with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, and that readable difference is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-epilogue: Neuropol looks digital, futuristic and closed. Epilogue, a plain sans with curvy, unclamped letters and a wire-like monoline skeleton, opens everything back up beneath it, so the page moves from tight outline to loose, tall-bodied text.
